title: Prototype Pollution in deep-defaults
longFix: The recursive merge had no guard on reserved keys; a `__proto__` key in the source recursed into and polluted `Object.prototype`. The merge now skips `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype`.
summary: `deep-defaults` recursively fills in defaults from a source object. With no guard on reserved property names, a source object parsed from untrusted JSON containing `__proto__` causes the recursion to walk into `Object.prototype` and add properties there, polluting every object in the process.
fixExplanation: Source keys naming a prototype slot (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`) are skipped, so untrusted data can never reach `Object.prototype`. All legitimate default-merging behavior is preserved (verified by the ported upstream behavior cases).
